# refs — agent guide

## Setup

`just setup` links `../nodes` when the checkout is a git worktree, then refuses a tree
where `../nodes/python/pyproject.toml` is missing, then copies `registry/` into the packages
(`just registry-sync`). Run it right after `git worktree add`.

## Gates

- `just test-one <args>`: pytest in `python/`, so paths are relative to it
  (`just test-one tests/test_dialect.py`); with `ts` first, vitest in `ts/`
  (`just test-one ts tests/dialect.test.ts`).
- `just test-fast`: affected-only (pytest-testmon, then `vitest --changed`), except that
  an uncommitted change under `fixtures/` or `registry/` runs the full suite, since neither
  selector follows the data files tests read. `just test`: the full suite, both languages
  (the TypeScript run builds the package first).
- `just check`: `ops-check`, `ops-docs check`, `registry-check`, ruff and pyright on
  `python/`, `tsc` and biome on `ts/`, and `tasks check`. `just gate` is `check` then `test`.
- The hooks in `.githooks/` run the same commands; the full suite runs at pre-push, as no
  CI is configured. Every recipe runs through `tools/tt`; do not call a test runner
  directly.

## Layout

- `docs/STANDARD.md`: the authority.
- `python/`, `ts/`: the two packages; `fixtures/`: the shared conformance oracles both read.
- `tools/`: vendored from ops; never edit in place. `tools/vendor_registry.py` is this
  project's own: `just registry-vendor <snapshot> <sha256>` runs it.
- `registry/`: the vendored Bioregistry snapshot in the pattern dialect, its
  `registry/SOURCES.toml` and the shared `registry/local-schemes.toml`; the one copy.
  `just registry-sync` copies it into `python/src/refs/data/` and `ts/data/` (gitignored),
  and `registry-check` compares the copies with it.
- `.githooks/`: git hooks; a fresh clone runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`. Beside
  the pre-commit and pre-push gates, `post-merge` and `post-checkout` run `just registry-sync`
  (post-checkout only on a branch checkout), so a merge or checkout that changes `registry/`
  does not leave the gitignored data copies stale for editable consumers.

## Rules

- Authority order: `docs/STANDARD.md`, then the code and its tests, then the dated design
  records. When anything disagrees with the standard, it wins, or it has a bug: fix it in
  the same change.
- Tier 1 is fixture-first: a change to the dialect, CURIE parsing, the registry format,
  lookup, collisions, the fingerprint, vocabularies or the facet starts as a row in
  `fixtures/` and a line in `docs/STANDARD.md`, then lands in Python and TypeScript in the
  same change (`docs/STANDARD.md` section 1). Tier 3 (`rewrite`, `samples`, the vendoring
  tool, `load_vocabularies`, `build_about`) may be one language with no standard change.
- The dialect rule: every stored pattern is in the pattern dialect (`docs/STANDARD.md`
  section 2). Never hand-edit `registry/bioregistry.json`, `registry/SOURCES.toml` or
  `fixtures/registry.verdicts.json`: change the rewrite rules or re-vendor with
  `just registry-vendor`, then update the pinned fingerprint in `fixtures/registry.json`.
  A pattern a rewrite cannot express is refused and recorded, never hand-patched.
- Module boundary: the identifier, dialect, registry and vocabulary modules import nothing
  from `nodes`; only the facet module does, and a test in each language enforces it. refs
  ships a facet and an invariant, never a kind.
- Boundary with resolvers: refs is offline. It never fetches, resolves an identifier to a
  term, or checks membership in a held vocabulary (quarry and beliefs do), and no code path
  branches on what an identifier means rather than on its prefix's declared grammar.
- Refusals are `RefsError` with a `kind` and, for a pattern, a 0-based code-point position;
  the facet's invariant raises nodes' `FacetError`. Fail early: an unknown prefix, a
  malformed id or a missing required release is an error, never a pass-through.
